Your team projects 69.0 with the armband on Haaland. He is the captain, 0.3 points clear of Salah, and carries modest upside—a 25% chance of 10 or more, though an 8% tail risk of 2 or fewer. That margin is slim enough that the vice-captain matters; if Haaland underperforms, Salah at 7.9 is your safety net.

Three Arsenal players form your heaviest club weight. Combined with two each from Liverpool and Manchester City, this shapes both your ceiling and your floor: a strong gameweek for any of these three clubs compounds, but so does weakness. Mykolenko on the bench at 3.1 is the best available cover, but you have no free transfer to shift if needed.

The bench projects only 10.7 across four players. Anderson and Muniz offer very little, and Pope at 2.3 will only play if Raya fails. This is the cost of packing your points into the eleven.

You are holding. No transfer move justified its cost against what you have, so the armband decision and Haaland's form are the gameweek.

Your eleven projects to 69.0 with the armband on Haaland. He is 0.3 ahead of Salah and carries modest but real upside—a quarter chance of double figures against the projection, though an 8% tail risk of blanking badly. The case for him is narrow but it stands.

You have three Arsenal players and two each from Liverpool and Manchester City. Concentration at Arsenal is a choice; the others are standard template. Your bench is thin. Mykolenko at 3.1 is your best reserve, but none of them threaten the eleven.

No transfer clears its cost this week. You hold with no free transfers left, so the squad as picked is what plays.

Your armband is safe. Haaland leads Salah by 0.3, and while the margin is tight, no alternative clears the cost of the move needed to make it. Hold him.

You have three Arsenal players and two each from Liverpool and Manchester City. That is more concentration than most, but it reflects their projections rather than a bet on fixtures—those spreads are genuine. Your bench is weak; Mykolenko at 3.1 is your only meaningful option if someone fails to start, and there is no free transfer to improve it.

Wood at 4.2 is the softest pick in your starting eleven, but moving him costs 4 points and the model found no replacement that justifies it. Palmer at 6.0 is close enough to Semenyo that either could have been chosen; neither is obviously wrong.

You are projected 60.8 without the armband and 69.0 with it. That is a solid week given the constraints.
